newsitem.title: UK: Palladium surges to highest prices in seven months.
newsitem.headline: Palladium surges to highest prices in seven months.

text.p: Palladium traded at its highest level since early May last year on Monday afternoon as funds moved in on the Nymex floor.
"The funds like the look of this sort of market," a dealer said as palladium traded around $135.55/$136.55 per ounce.
"It all happened on the floor this afternoon. But there is not really a fresh factor around," he added.
Fund buying came in on the back of consumer covering against the continuing delay to the start of Russian-Japanse talks on settling their 1997 supply contract.
"Palladium is generally forecast to go higher because of the Russian issue," another dealer said.,

Palladium is a fairly shallow, low volume market -- world demand in 1995 totalled 6.1 million ounces according to leading platinum group metals refiner Johnson Matthey -- so the price would move on even light buying by just a couple of hedge funds, dealers said.
This afternoon palladium was fixed at $134.25, its highest fixing since July 23, 1996.
"Palladium is propping up platinum and gold this afternoon," one dealer said.
Russia is the world's leading supplier providing over 66 percent of needs while Japan accounted for over 40 percnt of demand in 1995.
It is used in electronic components, autocatalysts to clean up car exhaust fumes, dentistry and a wide variety of chemical applications.
